saml.description: ZITADEL supports only SP-initiated SAML flows when acting as a SAML identity provider/broker.
saml.note: IdP-initiated attempts failing are by design and should not be reported as flow-coherence bugs.

saml.description: Access tokens are opaque by default rather than JWTs.
saml.note: Tests that expect JWT claims directly in the access token will misinterpret normal opaque-token behavior as a bug.

saml.description: When token exchange requests an ID token, ZITADEL returns it in the access_token response field and sets token_type to N_A.
saml.note: This looks odd but follows RFC 8693 behavior as implemented by ZITADEL; do not use that field as a bearer token.

saml.description: Introspection reports active only when the requesting client is part of the token audience.
saml.note: An inactive result from the wrong client does not mean the token itself is invalid.

saml.description: SAML SSO endpoint errors are conveyed inside the SAML response StatusCode while the HTTP status remains 200.
saml.note: Do not treat HTTP 200 from the SAML SSO endpoint as proof of successful authentication.

saml.description: The SAML SSO endpoint uses HTTP 200 even when the SAML response contains an error StatusCode.
saml.note: Tests must inspect SAML status content, not only HTTP status.

saml.constraint: ZITADEL supports only SP-initiated SAML flow. The fuzzer MUST start from the OIDC authorization endpoint and let ZITADEL redirect into the external SAML IdP flow; do NOT test IdP-initiated SAML because the docs state ZITADEL supports only SP-initiated flow.

For SAML brokering tests that expect a downstream API bearer token, the sequence MUST include start_oidc_auth followed by exchange_code_for_token. The SAML assertion is consumed inside ZITADEL's browser flow; there is no documented standalone SAML ACS login endpoint that directly returns an API bearer token.

ZITADEL does not support Resource Owner Password Credentials grant. Do NOT expect login_with_password for admin or user setup via /oauth/v2/token; use other documented auth methods such as client credentials, private_key_jwt, PAT, or interactive browser flows.

For I2 freshness tests on JWT-based client authentication and JWT profile grants, client_assertion/private-key JWT iat MUST NOT be older than 1 hour, and aud MUST include ZITADEL's issuing domain. Use dynamic claims such as iat={{now_epoch}} and exp={{now_epoch_plus_3600}}; otherwise failures may be due to malformed client authentication rather than the target invariant.

For I2 expired_token and future_token tests against token-bearing flows, include a CONTROL request using a valid token/assertion alongside the attack request. Without a control, invalid_grant or invalid_client cannot be distinguished from broken client authentication or bad app configuration.

Token exchange audience is restrictive by design: requested audience MUST be a subset of the combined audiences from subject_token and actor_token. The fuzzer MUST provision subject/actor tokens whose audiences already include the target audience before testing audience enforcement; otherwise rejection is expected and not a bug.

Token exchange scope behavior is permissive by design: requested scope can differ from supplied token scope, but invalid_scope is returned if it exceeds what ZITADEL allows. For I5 scope-escalation tests, compare the exchanged token's actual scope/claims to the requested scope and upstream authorization, not merely whether the request was accepted.
The token exchange resource parameter is currently not supported and supplying it results in invalid_target. The fuzzer MUST NOT use resource to model audience tests on ZITADEL; use audience instead.

When requested_token_type=urn:ietf:params:oauth:token-type:id_token in token exchange, ZITADEL returns the ID token in the access_token field and sets token_type=N_A. The fuzzer MUST NOT treat that returned access_token field as a bearer token for API calls; use requested_token_type access_token or jwt when a session bearer is needed.

ZITADEL access tokens are opaque by default. The fuzzer MUST use /oidc/v1/userinfo or /oauth/v2/introspect for verification instead of assuming local JWT parsing will work. If a JWT access token is required for a test, explicitly request JWT token type where documented.

Introspection returns active=true only if the token is active AND the requesting client is part of the token audience. For verification, the fuzzer MUST introspect with a client that belongs to the token audience; otherwise inactive/401 can be expected and is not evidence of token invalidity.

Reserved organization scope urn:zitadel:iam:org:id:{id} enforces that the user is a member of the selected organization. For multi-tenant or cross-org tests, the fuzzer MUST account for this scope because adding it intentionally narrows who can authenticate; omitting it broadens login behavior.

Reserved scope urn:zitadel:iam:org:domain:primary:{domainname} requires exact organization membership and exact username suffix by the provided domain. This is exact string semantics, not wildcard matching. For multi-identity I4 tests, omit this scope unless every tested identity is intended to share that exact domain suffix.

Reserved scope urn:zitadel:iam:org:roles:id:{orgID} limits returned organization IDs in role claims and ignores unknown organization IDs. For I5 authorization-binding tests involving role claims, do not interpret missing roles for unknown org IDs as a bug; unknown IDs are ignored by design.

For SAML external IdP login on Login V2, user creation can fail unless required fields are mapped from SAML attributes via Actions V2 on /zitadel.user.v2.UserService/RetrieveIdentityProviderIntent. The fuzzer MUST ensure required attributes such as email, first name, and last name are available/mapped before treating login failure as a SAML security rejection.

SAML provider setup commonly relies on metadata import and may preconfigure signing/binding details from metadata. For SAML signature-validation tests, the fuzzer MUST distinguish failures caused by metadata/config mismatch from failures caused by assertion validation. Use provider metadata that matches the intended ACS/entity IDs before mutating only the security-relevant assertion fields.

ZITADEL supports both opaque and JWT subject_token values for token exchange access_token type, but refresh_token is not allowed as subject_token or actor_token. The fuzzer MUST NOT use refresh tokens in token exchange replay or audience tests; use refresh_token grant separately.

ZITADEL supports only SP-initiated SAML flow. Do NOT attempt IdP-initiated SAML tests against ZITADEL as SP; a valid SAML test MUST begin by initiating the SP flow so the response can carry the matching InResponseTo/request context.

For saml_login, the executor MUST first initiate the SAML flow and obtain a SAML request ID, then POST to /v2/saml/saml_requests/{saml_request_id}. A fabricated standalone SAMLResponse without prior flow state will be rejected because ZITADEL binds finalization to an existing SAML request and session.

SAML login finalization requires an Authorization header from an account permitted with the IAM_LOGIN_CLIENT role, and the request body must include the latest session.sessionId and session.sessionToken. Do NOT treat the SAMLResponse alone as sufficient proof; the flow is session-bound.

The SSO endpoint /saml/v2/SSO returns HTTP 200 even on SAML errors; failure is conveyed inside the SAML StatusCode/message, not via HTTP status. Do NOT interpret HTTP 200 from SAML endpoints as successful authentication in I1/I5 tests.

For SAML brokered user creation in Login V2, required user fields are not auto-populated from SAML attributes by default. Tests expecting first-login provisioning MUST configure an Actions V2 response manipulation on /zitadel.user.v2.UserService/RetrieveIdentityProviderIntent to map attributes like email/firstName/lastName, otherwise login may fail for setup reasons unrelated to the security property under test.

For I4 SAML identity-binding tests, ZITADEL commonly maps external IdP information into local user creation/linking fields via actions, often using email as username/UserName/IdpLinks.UserName. Tests for saml_email_binding_collision and cross-protocol merges MUST control both NameID and mapped email attributes, because email-based linking may be intentionally configured by the deployment rather than being an SP parser bug.

For organization-scoped external IdP tests, the authorization request MUST include the reserved scope urn:zitadel:iam:org:id:{id} when organization settings override default settings. Without the org scope, ZITADEL may show/use default IdPs and login policy, causing false positives in SAML provider-selection and policy tests.

Token exchange audience is restrictive: requested audience MUST be a subset of the combined audiences from subject_token and actor_token. For I5 token_exchange_wrong_audience and token_exchange_ignore_audience tests, first obtain a control token whose audience includes the target; otherwise rejection is expected by design and not evidence of stronger validation bugs.

Token exchange scope behavior is by design permissive in one direction: requested scope can be changed and may be extended or decreased, but invalid or excessive scope yields invalid_scope and the final granted scope may differ from the requested scope. I5 scope-escalation tests MUST compare the returned scope/claims, not just request acceptance.
The token exchange resource parameter is not supported and supplying it results in invalid_target. Do NOT use resource to model audience-binding tests on ZITADEL; use the audience parameter instead.

When requested_token_type=id_token in token exchange, the returned ID token is placed in the access_token field and token_type is N_A. The fuzzer MUST NOT use that value as a Bearer session token for verify_granted_identity or other API calls; request an access token or JWT token type with openid scope if a usable bearer token plus ID token is needed.

ZITADEL introspection returns active=true only if the token is active and the requesting client is part of the token audience. I5 audience-binding tests using introspection MUST authenticate as a client that is in the token audience for control cases; otherwise active=false is expected by design.

For JWT-based client authentication to token or introspection endpoints, aud MUST include ZITADEL's issuing domain and iat MUST NOT be older than 1 hour. Freshness failures in these client assertions are setup errors, not target-protocol vulnerabilities.

Numeric sentinel: LDAP provider timeout has special meaning for zero. timeout=0s does NOT mean immediate timeout; it selects the default timeout of 60s. Never assume zero disables waiting or creates a strict zero-duration check.

For I2 freshness tests on OIDC tokens, include a control login using a valid token/code path and compare against the attack case. ZITADEL returns HTTP 401 for invalid or expired userinfo tokens and standard OAuth errors for token endpoint failures; without a control, LOGIN_FAILED may reflect broken client authentication or redirect mismatch rather than freshness enforcement.
ZITADEL supports only SP-initiated SAML flows. Do NOT attempt IdP-initiated SAML tests against ZITADEL as the broker/SP side; such failures are by design and not I3/I1 bugs.

For SAML programmatic/custom-login flows, the executor MUST first initialize the SAML request and obtain a request_id, then finalize it at POST /v2/saml/saml_requests/{request_id}. A fabricated standalone SAML POST without a bound request_id/InResponseTo will be rejected for flow reasons, not necessarily because signature or issuer validation worked.

SAML SSO endpoint errors are returned with HTTP 200 and encoded in the SAML StatusCode/message. Do NOT treat HTTP 200 from /saml/v2/SSO as authentication success; parse the SAML response content or downstream token issuance result.

Login V2 / programmatic SAML brokering requires required user fields to be present for just-in-time user creation. Without Actions V2 mapping on /zitadel.user.v2.UserService/RetrieveIdentityProviderIntent, SAML logins may fail due to missing mapped attributes rather than security enforcement. Configure attribute mapping for email, first name, last name, and username before testing broker acceptance.

External IdP logins must be allowed in the login policy (default or organization-specific) and the provider must be activated/linked to that login policy. Otherwise SAML login failures are setup failures, not security rejections.

Token exchange audience can only be reduced, never expanded: requested audience MUST be a subset of the combined audiences from subject_token and actor_token. Cross-project or cross-organization audience escalation attempts that fail are by design, not I5 bugs.

Token exchange scope may differ from the requested scope because ZITADEL validates and may reduce it. For I5 scope-escalation tests, compare the returned scope/claims, not just whether the request was accepted.

The token exchange response may place a requested ID token into the access_token field and set token_type=N_A. The fuzzer MUST NOT use session_token as a Bearer credential when issued_token_type is urn:ietf:params:oauth:token-type:id_token or token_type is N_A; request access_token or jwt token type for subsequent API calls.

ZITADEL rejects refresh_token as subject_token/actor_token in token exchange. Do NOT use refresh tokens for replay or audience-binding token-exchange tests; use access_token or id_token as documented.

For impersonation token-exchange tests, instance security must allow impersonation and the actor must hold an impersonation role. Otherwise rejection is expected and not evidence of correct/incorrect subject binding.

When using JWT-based client authentication or JWT profile grants, aud MUST include ZITADEL's issuing domain and iat MUST NOT be older than 1 hour. Expired/old assertions will fail for freshness reasons unrelated to the target invariant.

ZITADEL access tokens are opaque by default. For verification and replay/freshness analysis, prefer introspection or userinfo rather than local JWT parsing unless the application/token exchange explicitly requested JWT access tokens.

Introspection returns active=true only if the requesting client is part of the token audience. A false/limited introspection result from the wrong client is not proof of token invalidity; use a client in the audience for verification.
The resource parameter in token exchange is not supported and returns invalid_target. Do NOT use resource-based audience tests against ZITADEL; use the audience parameter instead.
